articles.title: High Court Rules Against Hopwood DePree in Ownership Dispute Over Hopwood Hall
articles.excerpt: The High Court in Manchester has ruled that Rochdale Council acted fairly in denying ownership of Hopwood Hall to Hopwood DePree, a descendant of the original owners.
articles.content_html:
A High Court in Manchester has ruled that Rochdale Council did not act unfairly in its decision not to transfer ownership of Hopwood Hall to Hopwood DePree, a descendant of the family that originally built the historic property in the 1420s. The ruling concluded a two-day trial concerning an exclusivity agreement that had been established for the sale of the Grade II-listed hall.

Mr DePree, who took legal action against the council, expressed disappointment following the verdict, stating it was a significant setback for both his family and the community. He noted that his team is currently exploring legal options for potential next steps. DePree emphasised the importance of Hopwood Hall to local heritage and pledged to monitor the council's efforts to preserve and restore the building.

Hopwood Hall has a rich history, having been owned by the Hopwood family until 1922, after which it changed hands several times. The property was used as a Catholic teacher training college until the 1980s and subsequently fell into disrepair. Rochdale Council acquired the hall and remains its owner today, with ongoing discussions about its future and restoration.

The court's decision marks a significant moment in the ongoing debate over the future of Hopwood Hall, which is not only a local landmark but also a site of historical importance. The ruling may influence future efforts to restore the hall and its surrounding grounds, which are now part of Hopwood Hall College.
